record.paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
record.original_question: Is the toric ideal of every smooth projectively normal toric variety generated by quadrics?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X \subset \mathbb{P}^N$ be a smooth projective toric variety that is projectively normal in its given embedding. Equivalently, let $P \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a smooth lattice polytope (i.e., a lattice polytope at each of whose vertices the primitive edge vectors form a basis of $\mathbb{Z}^n$) such that for every positive integer $k$, every lattice point of $kP$ is a sum of $k$ lattice points of $P$ (so the associated projective toric variety $X_P$ is projectively normal). Let $I_P \subset k[x_a : a \in P \cap \mathbb{Z}^n]$ denote the toric ideal defining $X_P$, that is, the kernel of the ring homomorphism sending $x_a$ to $t^a \cdot s$ in the polynomial ring $k[t_1^{\pm 1},\dots,t_n^{\pm 1},s]$.

Prove or disprove: the ideal $I_P$ is generated by quadratic binomials.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the toric ideal of every smooth projectively normal toric variety is generated by quadrics (a conjecture attributed to Bøgvad / Sturmfels) is widely cited as open. Workshops dedicated to projective normality and quadratic generation of smooth toric varieties (Oberwolfach 2007, AIM 2009) treat it as an open problem, and no proof or counterexample appears in the literature as of recent surveys.

status_evidence.snippet: Workshop devoted to open problems about projective normality and quadratic generation of ideals of smooth toric varieties.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is treated as open by the research community.

status_evidence.claim: Status remains open as of recent dedicated workshops.
